_note: Mockup of the Day 1 Response fight. Numbers come from notes.json (response_combat.scaling): player HP 90, boss HP 85. The deck and the upgrades come from Hardening (the save's deck and equipped_passives); there is no choice here. Each pattern has one upgrade that counters it (counter). With it the pattern plays as written; without it the pattern uses its harsh numbers instead (denser, harder-hitting, or a shorter warning), so a skipped counter costs HP even for a player who dodges well. lockout stops the stream after a number of failed tries, unique stops one hit from opening every account, twostep blocks most of a stolen-password hit, alerts gives a longer warning. A pattern's kind picks how the bullets are made: stream (random heights, one by one, all in one direction), sweep (a wall with a gap that walks through gaps), aimed (a line warns, then a key flies along it; every volley_every shots a fan of volley_count keys). works / missing are the lines shown after the pattern when that upgrade was / was not equipped. say is what the threat says first. box is the size of the arena, lead the seconds a bullet is in sight before it reaches the box.

defenses.name: Unique passwords
defenses.works: Only one account was hit. Every other account kept its own password, so the damage stayed small.
defenses.missing: One password opened every account. Unique passwords would have kept the damage to one.

defenses.name: Two-step sign-in
defenses.works: The stolen password was not enough. The second step (a code) stopped most of each hit.
defenses.missing: The stolen password opened the door alone. A second sign-in step would have stopped it.

defenses.name: Lock after failed tries
defenses.works: The account locked after a few wrong tries and the guessing stopped.
defenses.missing: The attacker guessed all turn long. Locking the account after a few wrong tries would have stopped it.

defenses.name: Unusual sign-in alerts
defenses.works: The alert gave you extra time to react to the stolen password.
defenses.missing: Nothing warned you early. An alert for unusual sign-ins would have given you time.

patterns.name: Rapid guesses
patterns.teach: The attacker tries password after password, very fast.

patterns.name: One password, many accounts
patterns.teach: One common password is tried on every account.
patterns.say: Summer2024. Let us see who still uses it.

patterns.name: Stolen password
patterns.teach: A leaked password works on the first try. No guessing needed.
patterns.say: No need to guess. I already have your password.
